_meta.name: trace
_meta.note: User-facing trace projection: the curated feed for the Portal/Studio trace UI. It shows WHAT happened (runs, agents, tools, public user prompts and assistant responses, timings, status), never HOW the platform decides. System/internal prompts and orchestration mechanics remain excluded, and sensitive values are scrubbed.

connection.event_received.drop_reason: Provider receipt data stays out of user-facing traces.

email.received.drop_reason: Email content stays out of user-facing traces.

conversation.reply_received.drop_reason: Conversation content stays out of user-facing traces.

memory.record_changed.note: Metadata-only durable memory change; record contents stay private.

trigger.fire_requested.drop_reason: The system-tool node already represents the request; admission lifecycle is authoritative.

assignment_received.note: A run (root or delegated child) enters the tree as a run node.

assignment_completed.note: A delegated run closes its node in the parent tree.

final.note: The run node completes with status success.

session.completed.note: Projected completion closes the run node.

error.note: The run node completes with status failed.

system_tool_start.note: A tool node opens; correlation_id pairs it with completion.

tool.dispatch_started.note: Projected dispatch start opens the tool node.

system_tool_complete.note: The tool node closes with status success and latency.

model_tool_complete.note: Deterministic model-tool completion closes its tool node.

tool_event.note: Legacy paired tool event closes the tool node.

tool.dispatch_completed.note: Projected dispatch completion closes the tool node.

system_tool_error.note: The tool node closes with status failed; the message is redacted upstream.

interrupt_request.note: The run is waiting on a human; the node shows the pause, not the question.

interrupt_required.note: Interrupt-required marker; same curated pause node.

trigger.fired.note: The trigger that started this run heads the tree.

evaluating.note: Curated by design: internal processing phases collapse into one working aspect - the trace shows THAT the platform was working, never how it decides.

update.drop_reason: Internal state delta; contents are inner workings.

progress_update.drop_reason: Internal progress accounting; usage lands on the run node instead. The trace assembler lifts only closed stages out of it: model-call lifecycle and decision_completed, which becomes trace.decision (model, duration and origin; never inputs or outputs).

status_message.drop_reason: Streaming narration; the trace is structural, not textual.

status_message_chunk.note: Client-safe final-response chunks contribute response text and streaming metrics to the model exchange.

system_tool_chunk.drop_reason: Intra-tool streaming; the tool node carries start/completion.

hook_fired.note: Developer-registered hook callback as run structure: which hook ran, at which stage, and whether it succeeded. Names and status only; nothing that passed through the hook.

trigger.skipped.note: A trigger that declined to fire explains why an expected run never happened, which is the hardest thing to debug from absence alone. Carries no user content.

trigger.failed.note: A trigger that failed is why the owner's automation did not run. That is their answer, not operational noise. Carries no user content.

trigger.disabled.drop_reason: Trigger admin lifecycle; not part of a run.

trigger.enabled.drop_reason: Trigger admin lifecycle; not part of a run.

agent.tool_selected.drop_reason: Canvas paint hint; the tool nodes carry the structure.

agent.responded.drop_reason: Canvas paint hint; run completion carries the structure.
